name: Arvind Krishna

career.organization: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center
career.title: Researcher, rising to research leadership roles
Senior Vice President; led the $34 billion Red Hat acquisition

background_rationale: An electrical engineering PhD who spent nearly two decades at IBM Research and led IBM's research, systems and cloud software businesses before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: In his first memo as CEO, during the COVID-19 pandemic, Krishna told employees that the crisis had shown IBM's essential role and that 'trust is our license to operate.'
Completed the spin-off of IBM's managed infrastructure services unit as Kyndryl, announced in October 2020, to focus IBM on hybrid cloud and AI.
Announced the acquisition of data-streaming company Confluent at an $11 billion valuation; the deal closed in March 2026.
IBM agreed to acquire HRL Laboratories to add expertise in silicon-spin qubits, quantum sensing and cryogenics.

personal_story.hook: Arvind Krishna joined IBM's research lab in 1990 and spent 30 years there before becoming CEO.
personal_story.summary: Krishna was born in 1962 in Andhra Pradesh, India, into a Telugu family; his father was an Indian Army officer who rose to major general. He attended schools in Coonoor, Tamil Nadu, and Dehradun, then earned an electrical engineering degree at IIT Kanpur in 1985. He moved to the U.S. for a PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and joined IBM's Thomas J. Watson Research Center in 1990, where he spent about 18 years. He later ran IBM Research and its cloud software business and was a principal architect of the $34 billion Red Hat acquisition, the deal that preceded his appointment as CEO in 2020.
